# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

`AGENTS.md` is a symlink to this file, so editing `CLAUDE.md` updates both.

## Generated files - never hand-edit

Both of these are build output, and edits to them are lost on the next build:

- `src/common/palette.js` is generated by `just build` from `templates/palette.tera` (requires `whiskers`). The template's `filename` frontmatter key is what directs output there
- `src/css/awoo.min.css` is generated by `just build-awoo-css` from `src/css/awoo-local.min.css`, with the Google Fonts `@import` prepended. Edit the local file, never the generated one

## Overview

A static, dependency-free browser startpage themed with the [Catppuccin](https://catppuccin.com/palette) palettes, served from GitHub Pages. Vanilla JavaScript Web Components loaded via plain `<script>` tags from `index.html` - no bundler, no package manager, no `package.json`, no runtime dependencies. See `README.md` for features and user-facing configuration.

## Commands

`just --list` for the full set, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` for the day-to-day table. `just format` / `just lint` / `just test` are deliberate no-ops - there is no formatter, linter, or test suite, hence the empty `.no-tests` marker - so `just check` effectively only runs `build`. There is no CI either: no GitHub Actions workflows exist, so verifying a behavioral change means loading the page in a browser via `just run-dev-server`.

## Architecture

### Load order matters

`index.html` loads scripts in a strict sequence, and everything downstream depends on globals defined upstream. Adding a new file means inserting it at the right point:

1. `src/common/palette.js` - defines the `latte` / `frappe` / `macchiato` / `mocha` palette objects as bare globals
2. `src/common/utils.js`, `storage.js`, `actions.js`, `config.js`, `strftime.js`, `theme.js`, `component.js` - the shared runtime
3. `userconfig.js` (untracked, but not listed in `.gitignore`; users copy it from `userconfig.example.js`) - picks the light/dark palettes, calls `initThemeSystem`, constructs the global `CONFIG = new Config(...)`, and sets the `:root` CSS variables `--bg` / `--accent` from the palette
4. An inline `<script>` in `index.html` that reads `CONFIG.localFonts` and injects the font/`awoo` stylesheet links
5. The component classes under `src/components/`
6. `src/common/module.js` - registers every component class as a custom element, last, because registration triggers rendering

`CONFIG` is a true global that every component reads directly at construction and render time. It must exist before any component class is registered.

### Component model

`src/common/component.js` defines `Component extends HTMLElement`, the base class for every registered component (`Links` and `Category` in `tabs.component.js` also extend it but are never registered or instantiated - they are static helper namespaces). Key mechanics:

- each component attaches an **open shadow root**, so all component CSS is written inline as a template string in `style()` and interpolates `CONFIG.palette.*` values directly, so most colors are baked in at render time. Two theme CSS variables do exist alongside that: `userconfig.js` sets `--bg` and `--accent` on `:root`, `src/css/style.css` consumes `--bg`, and `tabs` / `statusbar` inherit `--accent` into their shadow roots as the default `--flavour`
- subclasses override `style()`, `template()`, and `imports()`; `render()` concatenates them into `shadow.innerHTML`
- `imports()` returns `<link>` tags obtained from `this.getResource(category, name)`. `getResource` consults `Component.localOverrides` and swaps in the local-font variant when `CONFIG.localFonts` is true, which is how the "no Google Fonts CDN" mode works
- `this.refs` is a Proxy over a plain selector map: declare `refs = { input: '#search input' }` and then read `this.refs.input` to get the live shadow-DOM element, or assign to it to set `innerHTML`
- `render()` registers the instance in the global `RenderedComponents` map keyed by tag name; `Actions.activate(name)` looks the instance up there and calls its `activate()`. This is the entire inter-component messaging layer, and it is what keybindings dispatch through

Components are registered in `src/common/module.js`. `CONFIG.disabled` is an array of tag names that are skipped at registration; the global CSS rule `*:not(:defined) { display: none }` hides the leftover markup.

Only `<tabs-list>` appears in `index.html`; everything else is nested inside shadow roots. `Statusbar` reaches out of its own shadow root via `this.parentNode.querySelectorAll(...)` into `externalRefs` to drive the tab panels that `Tabs` rendered. Tab switching sets an `active` attribute on both the indicator `<li>` in the statusbar and the matching `<ul>` in the tabs panel; the CSS does the rest. Any change to the tabs markup has to keep that parent/child selector coupling intact.

### Configuration

`Config` (`src/common/config.js`) merges three sources per top-level key, in this precedence:

1. `userconfig.js`, but only when `overrideStorage` is true or the key is `tabs` (`tabs` always wins)
2. `localStorage` under the `configuration` key, via the `Storage` wrapper
3. the `defaults` object literal in `Config`

The constructor returns a `Proxy`, so any assignment to a `CONFIG` property re-persists the whole object to `localStorage`. When adding a new setting, add it to `defaults` in `config.js` **and** to `userconfig.example.js`, otherwise it will never be picked up by `autoConfig`.

`userconfig.js` is a user file that is not in the repo; `userconfig.example.js` is the template and the de-facto documentation of the schema.

Two known traps, so they are not mistaken for something a change broke: `Config.setKeybindings` reads the raw userconfig object rather than the merged `CONFIG`, so a `userconfig.js` with no `keybindings` key throws there; and `localIcons` appears in `userconfig.example.js` and the README but is read nowhere in the source.

### Theme switching

`initThemeSystem(light, dark)` in `src/common/theme.js` reads `prefers-color-scheme`, returns the matching palette object, and installs a `change` listener that reloads the page on system theme switches - because component styles are baked in at render time, a reload is the switching mechanism.

### Fonts and icons

Two parallel sets of stylesheets exist throughout: CDN variants and `-local` variants. `CONFIG.localFonts` selects between them in two places that must stay in sync - the inline loader in `index.html` and `Component.localOverrides`.

### Date formatting

`src/common/strftime.js` extends `Date.prototype` with a percent-less `strftime` and adds `Date.createWithTimezone(ianaName)`. The clock format tokens used in configs (`k`, `i`, `p`, `h`, `H`, `K`) are defined in the `formats` map there, not in the clock component.

## Conventions

- comments use British spellings ("colour", "initialise", "customisable") throughout the source; match it
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` carries the commit, branch, and pull request conventions
